summary: Rutland County, VT: tower built about 1914 by timberland owner Newton Chaffee, rebuilt 1915, removed in 1974 as unsafe; site now in Mt. Carmel State Forest.

facts.agency: Newton Chaffee, a timberland owner (private), per the 1914 construction account
facts.status_note: FPR says removed in 1974 for unsafe condition; Forest Lookouts says toppled over (no date); FFLOS lists it as gone

access.note: State forest with no deeded access; reached on foot by the New Boston Trail, a side trail of the Long Trail (FPR). The summit remains are not described.

visit.trail_note: Reached by the New Boston Trail, a side trail of the Long Trail, with no deeded access (FPR); trails maintained by the Green Mountain Club (FPR).

events.note: Constructed c.1914 by Newton Chaffee (Forest Lookouts, quoting History of Forestry in Vermont); FPR also gives 1914
Reconstruction of the tower made possible by Chaffee, per the 8th Annual Report of the Vermont State Forester as quoted by Forest Lookouts; telephone line to the summit not yet built
FPR says removed in 1974 due to unsafe condition. A Rutland Daily Herald notice of 2 August 1974 still refers to the tower. Forest Lookouts says it toppled over, without a date.

evidence.quote: Mr. Newton Chaffee constructed a tower on Mt. Carmel.

evidence.supports: 1915 reconstruction made possible by Chaffee, who owned timberland
evidence.quote: Mr. Chaffee, who owns considerable timberland in this section, made possible the reconstruction of the tower on Mount Carmel.

evidence.supports: no telephone line to the summit yet
evidence.quote: No telephone, however, has as yet been constructed.

evidence.supports: 2 Aug 1974 hike notice still refers to the fire tower (existence in 1974, not its condition)
evidence.quote: There are good views from the Mt. Carmel Fire Tower.

evidence.supports: built 1914, removed 1974 due to unsafe condition
evidence.quote: A fire tower was constructed on top of Mt. Carmel in 1914 but was removed in 1974 due to its unsafe condition.

evidence.supports: state forest, 263 acres, gift in 1956 from Governor Redfield Proctor
evidence.quote: The Mt. Carmel State Forest was a 263-acre gift to the State of Vermont in 1956 from Governor Redfield Proctor.

evidence.supports: no deeded access; access by New Boston Trail
evidence.quote: While there is no deeded access to the forest it can be accessed by the New Boston Trail, a side trail to the Long Trail.

evidence.supports: trails maintained by Green Mountain Club
evidence.quote: The trails are maintained by the Green Mountain Club.

evidence.supports: state forest reaches the summit of Mt. Carmel (now part of the forest)
evidence.quote: Elevation of the forest range from 2380 to 3365 feet at the summit of Mt. Carmel.

sources.title: Mt. Carmel State Forest
sources.publisher: Vermont Department of Forests, Parks and Recreation (fpr.vermont.gov)

corrections.why: c.1914 is a construction date, not an agency. Forest Lookouts, quoting History of Forestry in Vermont, names Newton Chaffee as the person who constructed the tower.

notes_for_editor: Two accounts of the end differ: FPR says removed in 1974 because unsafe; Forest Lookouts says 'Toppled over.' with no date. Not reconciled; the story says so. The 1915 report and 1914 build date both come through secondary quotes (Forest Lookouts), not primary documents. The 1974 Herald notice is cited only through Forest Lookouts. Status 'gone' from FFLOS and FPR agree in substance. Kind 'platform' matches FFLOS 'Open Tower' (vocab: open tower or platform, no cab). Budget: 2 WebSearch calls (second found no newspaper text), 4 page reads (Forest Lookouts, FFLOS index, FPR, Wikipedia for context only). No photos found. Access: public trail access, no road, no deeded access per FPR.
